title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 163 (Option to adopt principle of proportional representation for appointment of directors)

content.overview: Section 163 allows the articles of a company to provide for appointment of not less than two-thirds of the total number of directors of a company according to the principle of proportional representation, whether by the single transferable vote or by a system of cumulative voting or otherwise. Such directors are not liable to retire by rotation.
content.glance: Articles may adopt proportional representation (STV, cumulative voting or otherwise) for ≥2/3 of directors; those directors are not liable to retire by rotation; s. 162 then does not apply.
content.study: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the articles of a company may provide for the appointment of not less than two-thirds of the total number of the directors of a company in accordance with the principle of proportional representation, whether by the single transferable vote or by a system of cumulative voting or otherwise and such appointments may be made once every three years and casual vacancies of such directors shall be filled as provided in the said articles. Such directors are not liable to retire by rotation. Section 162 (individual voting) does not apply where this system is adopted. Current-law framing: check whether articles adopt proportional representation for at least two-thirds of directors; apply the article system and non-rotation consequence.

sections.heading: Enabling Power
sections.body: Articles may provide for appointment of not less than two-thirds of the total number of directors by proportional representation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.body: Single transferable vote, cumulative voting, or otherwise as the articles specify.

sections.heading: Tenure and Casual Vacancy
sections.body: Appointments may be made once every three years; casual vacancies are filled as provided in the articles.

sections.heading: No Rotation
sections.body: Directors appointed under this system are not liable to retire by rotation under section 152.

provisions.title: Option to adopt principle of proportional representation for appointment of directors

examples.title: Articles adopt STV
examples.body: Articles provide that two-thirds of directors are elected by single transferable vote every three years. Those directors are not rotational under s. 152, and s. 162 does not apply to their election.

examples.title: No article provision
examples.body: Articles are silent on proportional representation. Section 163 is not engaged; ordinary appointment and rotation under ss. 152 and 162 apply.

hypotheticals.question: Must every company use proportional representation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 163 is enabling. It applies only if the articles so provide for not less than two-thirds of the directors.

distinctions.title: Proportional representation (s. 163) vs ordinary rotation (s. 152)
distinctions.left: Optional article-based proportional election; no rotation for those directors
distinctions.right: Default public-company rotation of ≥2/3 of directors

misconceptions.trap: Proportional representation is mandatory for all public companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 163 is an option the articles may adopt; it is not a mandatory system.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 163 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check articles for proportional representation of ≥2/3 directors. II. Apply method and three-year cycle. III. Note non-rotation and s. 162 carve-out. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article text; method used; tenure facts; precise relief.
